key_insight: A polymorphic high-entropy oxide photocatalyst combined with microalgae as a sacrificial agent dramatically boosts solar-driven CO2 reduction to CO and CH4.
engineering_relevance: The study suggests a scalable route for improving photocatalytic carbon conversion by coupling catalyst design with a carbon-negative biomass scavenger.
method: Design an AB2O6-type high-entropy oxide, (Cs1/7Ba4/7Bi2/7)(Nb1/2Ta1/2)2O6, with layered perovskite/pyrochlore bi-polymorphy.
Use Cs and Ba to increase CO2 adsorption, Bi to promote polarization/charge separation, and Nb/Ta for charge transport.
Compare CO2 conversion performance with no sacrificial agent, microplastics, and microalgae.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that adding microalgae increases CO and CH4 production by 10-fold and 4-fold, respectively, relative to the HEO-only system.
watch_item: The approach depends on managing biological variability and reaction compatibility so microalgae remain effective and practical under real operating conditions.
paper_title: Sustainable photocatalytic CO2 conversion using microalgae as a carbon-negative scavenger
